key: USB AUDIO OUT TRACKS MAIN CUE
name: USB Audio

author.name: Mark Roberts
credits: Mark Roberts (markandrus/octemu): USB audio and MIDI implementation, MIT
Bryan T (bryantysinger): MAIN/CUE channels and hardware alignment findings
Sam Banks: octabam port, layouts and stream alignment

presentation.label: 20 CHANNELS
presentation.summary: Record eight stereo tracks, MAIN and CUE over USB at 44.1 kHz and 24 bits.
presentation.overview: This is octabam’s 20-channel USB output implementation. At high speed it sends each track after its effects and before its fader, plus the final MAIN and CUE buses. At full speed it sends the tracks’ stereo sum. Required USB MIDI support is included in the SDK source.
highlights: 20 channels at high speed: eight tracks plus MAIN and CUE
Recorded hardware evidence on both MKI and MKII
usage: Connect the Octatrack’s USB port to your recording host and choose its USB audio input. Use high-speed USB for all twenty channels.
Channels 1–16 are track 1–8 stereo pairs, 17–18 MAIN, and 19–20 CUE. Track channels are post-effects and pre-fader; MAIN/CUE include the mixdown.
Allow the stream to settle before recording: upstream reports reordered startup samples around 0.5–1.5 seconds after opening. Full-speed USB carries a stereo track sum.

limitations: USB output only. Host-to-Octatrack USB input variants are outside this import.
Requires the included internal USB MIDI dependency. Only one USB output layout can be composed.
USB MIDI clock sets the tempo since 0.1.3. The high-speed USB MIDI receive transfer stays at 64 bytes; octabam's 512-byte transfer is not included.
Windows and Linux hosts have not been measured in this record.
A startup sample-reordering burst remains open. Master-on MAIN remains 32 samples behind track taps; toggling master can leave up to 32 stale CUE frames.

storage.label: Audio rings
storage.conditions: Two rings: 1,024 × 80 bytes plus 1,024 × 8 bytes = 90,112 bytes (88 KiB). Four 32-byte dTDs and four 960-byte packet buffers add 3,968 bytes, before code and MIDI state.

processing.label: CPU load
processing.conditions: Upstream records sustained hardware captures and MIDI traffic, not a comparable hardware CPU utilization percentage.

impact.conditions: Audio modules are rated for an active instance, including expensive modes and changing controls; MIDI/USB features are rated while enabled. More tracks or instances increase demand. Shared runtime reservations and reused stock buffers are not added again per module. These rough source-backed tiers do not establish hardware headroom or qualification.

cpu.rationale: The CPU producer continuously copies twenty audio channels into rings and services high-speed USB packet/DMA completion alongside MIDI. The high tier reflects that sustained maximum-channel workload; CPU headroom is not quantitatively established.

dsp.rationale: The documented stream taps the existing DSP/CPU exchange and MAIN/CUE output words. It does not add a new DSP audio algorithm. Minimal is an estimate of additional DSP work, not zero bus or system contention.

memory.rationale: Audio rings occupy 88 KiB and DMA descriptors/packet buffers add 3,968 bytes before code and MIDI state. This is a moderate shared feature footprint relative to scalar/control modules and multi-instance reverb rings. Version 0.1.3 adds the 2,028-byte USB MIDI receive unit (usbmidi_rx).

tests.summary: Selected for the broadest recorded hardware evidence: MKI and MKII, sustained multi-track 24-bit captures and high MIDI receive traffic. The latest source includes track/MAIN alignment and a hardware-tested master-on CUE correction; startup artifacts and unmeasured host/platform cases remain. Octamod native and actual-browser composition/packaging parity and rejection checks passed on 1 October 2026. The owner reported both combined test images working; this is a smoke report, not full feature/load qualification.

steps: Include USB Audio in the firmware configuration. This source import is still pending verification.
Connect the Octatrack’s USB port to your recording host using high-speed USB for all twenty channels.
Choose the Octatrack USB audio input in your recording software. Channels 1–16 are the eight track stereo pairs, 17–18 MAIN and 19–20 CUE.
Allow the stream to settle before recording; upstream reports reordered startup samples around 0.5–1.5 seconds after opening.
access.noUiReason: This automatic USB output contribution adds no dedicated OT page, chooser entry or panel controls. Access is through the USB connection and the host’s audio input selector. The reviewer must verify this absence of OT UI against the pinned source before publication.
